name: Create Maximum Intensity Z-Stack Projection
description:
You have access to Fiji with a Z-stack microscopy image.

Your task is to create a maximum intensity projection from a Z-stack image:

1. Open the T1 Head sample image via File > Open Samples > T1 Head (2.4M, 16-bits)
   - This is a CT scan stack with multiple slices through a human head

2. Create a maximum intensity projection:
   - Go to Image > Stacks > Z Project...
   - Projection type: Max Intensity
   - Start slice: 1
   - Stop slice: (use the maximum, should be around 129)
   - Click OK to create the projection

3. Adjust the brightness and contrast for better visibility:
   - Go to Image > Adjust > Brightness/Contrast
   - Click 'Auto' to automatically adjust the contrast
   - Close the Brightness/Contrast window

4. Save the projection:
   - Go to File > Save As > PNG...
   - Save to ~/Fiji_Data/results/max_projection.png
   - Click Save

5. Measure the image statistics:
   - Make sure the projection image is selected
   - Go to Analyze > Measure (or press Ctrl+M)
   - This will show statistics in the Results window

6. Save the measurements:
   - In the Results window, go to File > Save As
   - Save to ~/Fiji_Data/results/projection_stats.csv

Expected Results:
- A maximum intensity projection image saved as PNG
- Statistics CSV file with mean, min, max intensity values
- The projection should show the brightest pixels from each Z position

Success Criteria:
- max_projection.png exists and is a valid image file
- projection_stats.csv exists with measurement data
- The projection image dimensions should be 256x256 (same XY as stack, but single slice)

metadata.data_source: Fiji built-in sample (T1 Head CT scan)
